units.label: Framework
units.title: Framework overview
units.question: What conceptual boundaries do I need before comparing historically different forms of mass killing?
units.cognitiveJob: Establish what the framework contains and which of its three units to enter. The overview orients; it does not itself teach the typology.

sources.note: Rendered in place as the framework's orientation.

caveats: The framework supplies a comparison vocabulary, not a legal classification system. Nothing on these screens establishes the legal status of a historical case.

units.label: Scope & purpose
units.title: Scope & purpose
units.question: What is Ares comparing, and what is deliberately outside its scope?
units.cognitiveJob: Scope & purpose stays on the framework overview: it is the orientation that makes the child units legible, and putting a navigation step before the publication's first substantive sentence would cost more than it saves.
units.note: A real child unit that has deliberately not been given its own screen. #51 prototypes one framework child only; promoting this to /framework/scope-purpose is #47 work and must not be inferred from this entry. Its caveats are the framework overview's caveats, shown on the parent surface it shares.

units.label: Definitions & typology
units.title: Definitions & typology
units.question: How can Ares compare forms of extreme mass killing without treating massacre, genocide and political slaughter as equivalent?
units.cognitiveJob: One job: acquire a comparison vocabulary and the distinctions that keep it honest. Three terms, one caveat set, one decision to continue.

sources.note: Question, terms and critical caveats authored for the guided layer in #45.
The canonical manuscript, offered on this screen as scholarly depth.

units.note: Caveats are not restated here because this screen renders the canonical set from mobile-reading-prototype.json (framework.criticalCaveats) in its own always-visible block. Restating them in the graph would create the second copy this contract exists to prevent.

units.label: Theoretical lenses
units.title: Theoretical lenses
units.question: Which theoretical lenses does Ares use, and what can each of them not explain?
units.cognitiveJob: Conceptual apparatus for the framework, opened on demand from the overview rather than stacked into the guided path.
units.note: A deferred split, documented rather than silently dropped. It remains a disclosure on the framework overview; promoting it to /framework/theoretical-lenses is #47 work.
